verdict.rationale: Hands-on community reports show the bulk-import half of the story works at scale: a 7M-article initial import, ~80M documents across 13 indexes once batch indexing arrived, and 1M records that 'just worked' on a small instance. One report says indexing of constantly changing records fell behind, but that concerns continuous updates rather than a one-off bulk load. The pack contains no evidence at all of async task tracking to know when indexing completes, and first-party docs only generically mention 'adding documents'. Missing for 10: any evidence of an async task API or status tracking for indexing completion, first-party docs on bulk/batch import throughput, guidance on the memory cost of large imports.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can bulk-import millions of documents quickly, with async task tracking to know when indexing completes

citations.quote: They needed a 16GB machine for the initial import because batch indexing is memory-intensive.
later releases plus batch indexing fixed it
sent 1,000,000 records; it "just worked" on an $8/mo Hetzner instance
